title: sdk(python): add standardized retry policy (429/5xx/transport) w/ exponential backoff, jitter, and retry budget
author: Monica Patel
release_notes: Python SDK now retries transient failures by default for non-streaming requests (429/5xx + certain transport errors) using exponential backoff with jitter and a bounded retry budget. Streaming requests are unchanged and are not retried by this PR.
description:
Summary: Implements the cross-SDK retry policy baseline in the Python SDK for Hosted API non-streaming requests. This addresses customer reports of "no retries" in Python (vs aggressive retries in TS) and aligns behavior with ADR-0137. Scope is intentionally limited to non-streaming calls; streaming disconnect/reconnect semantics are handled separately (see follow-up PR-415).

Motivation / context: Support has flagged multiple cases where transient gateway errors (429 bursts during deploys, occasional 503 flaps, and connection resets from proxies) cause immediate hard failures in Python while TS/Go clients behave differently (SUP-9334 and related threads). The goal is to make retry behavior predictable and safe: avoid retry storms, respect server hints (Retry-After), and bound total additional latency with a retry budget.

Behavior (new defaults): 1) Retryable HTTP status codes: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504. 2) Retryable transport errors: connection reset, DNS resolution failures, TLS handshake errors, and read timeouts where no response headers were received (requests.exceptions.ConnectionError / Timeout variants depending on transport adapter). 3) Non-retryable: all 4xx except 429; 408 is treated as non-retryable for now (too easy to misclassify long-running server work) until timeout semantics are fully unified in PR-413. 4) Exponential backoff w/ jitter: base_delay=0.5s, factor=2.0, max_delay=8.0s, full jitter applied per attempt. 5) Max attempts: 4 total (1 initial + up to 3 retries). 6) Retry budget: default max_elapsed_time=20s across retries (hard cap). When the remaining budget is exhausted, we surface a RetryExhaustedError that includes attempts, last status/error, and request_id (if available).

Server hint handling: For 429/503 responses, we respect Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date). When present, the computed sleep is min(retry_after, max_delay) and still counts against the retry budget. If Retry-After is unparseable, we fall back to exponential backoff.

Idempotency / safety: This PR does NOT change API surface area, but it does add an idempotency key strategy to make retries safer for POST inference calls. For non-streaming endpoints, the client now auto-attaches an Idempotency-Key header when retries are enabled and the caller did not provide one. The key is stable across attempts for the same request invocation (UUID4), preventing duplicate execution/billing on gateway retries where supported. Callers can override via per-request headers. (This aligns with the client retry + idempotency guidelines reviewed with Platform.)

Configuration & hooks: Adds RetryConfig (client-level) with per-request overrides. Settings: enabled, max_attempts, max_elapsed_time, base_delay, max_delay, retry_on_statuses, retry_on_methods (defaults to POST only for this SDK since primary endpoints are POST), and a retry_event_hook callback for lightweight telemetry (attempt, delay, reason, status_code, request_id). Hook is opt-in and defaults to None.

Changed areas (high level): - redwood/_client.py: wire RetryPolicy into request execution path for non-streaming endpoints only; ensure request-id propagation from responses. - redwood/_retries.py (new): classifier + backoff/jitter + retry budget accounting; Retry-After parsing. - redwood/_errors.py: add RetryExhaustedError and normalize transport error wrapping so callers can reliably inspect .cause. - docsstrings/examples: add a short snippet showing how to customize retry config and how to disable retries.

Illustrative example (added to examples/ and docstrings): client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"], retry=RetryConfig(max_attempts=6, max_elapsed_time=30, retry_event_hook=log_retry)) response = client.responses.create(model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b", input="...")

Tests: Adds unit tests with a mocked transport layer simulating: (a) 429 with Retry-After followed by success, (b) 503 flapping then success within budget, (c) repeated ConnectionError leading to RetryExhaustedError, (d) non-retryable 400/401 behavior, (e) idempotency key stability across attempts, and (f) budget enforcement with deterministic backoff (jitter stubbed).

Operational considerations / guardrails: - Backoff uses full jitter to reduce synchronization across clients (per SRE guidance). - Budget + max_attempts prevent unbounded latency amplification. - We do not retry streaming requests in this PR to avoid surprising partial-output semantics.

Follow-ups: - PR-413 will standardize timeout defaults and error mapping; once landed we can revisit 408 behavior and timeout-classified retries in a more controlled way. - PR-415 will implement streaming disconnect handling and explicitly define what is surfaced vs retried.

Review notes / discussion highlights: - Rafael requested the retry budget hard cap and full-jitter implementation to reduce retry amplification; added in commit 3. - Amara confirmed Retry-After behavior and header casing; we now parse both Retry-After and fall back cleanly. - Brian asked that we avoid retrying on 409/422 even if some APIs use them transiently; we keep the whitelist explicit.

Commits (squash-merged): 1) Add retry classifier + backoff/jitter + Retry-After parsing 2) Wire retry policy into client request path + add idempotency key generation 3) Add RetryExhaustedError + error wrapping for transport exceptions 4) Unit tests for status/transport/budget/idempotency scenarios 5) Update examples + docstrings

CI: python-unit (pass), python-lint (pass), type-check (pass), examples-smoke (pass).

Merge method: Squash and merge.
